newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: World-record holder dives to 515 feet on two breaths.
newsitem.headline: World-record holder dives to 515 feet on two breaths.

text.p: Cuban-born Francisco "Pipin" Ferraras dove on just two breaths to a new free-dive world record of 515 feet (157 metres) but stopped short of his original 600-foot (183-metre) goal.

Ferraras, already the free-dive record holder of 439 feet (134 metres) on one breath, said just before his dive on Saturday that he was trimming his goal to 500 feet (152 metres) due to safety considerations.

On May 15, Ferreras was rushed to a hospital and placed in a recompression chamber after passing out on a dive boat shortly after making a 450-foot (137-metre) practice free dive followed by a scuba dive.
According to members of Ferraras' support team, the 35-year-old reached 515 feet (157 metres) using a weighted sled to pull him down quickly.
Nancy Romanica, an organiser of the event, said the 515-foot (157 metres) mark was a new world record. His previous record was set last year in Mexico.
Ferreras, who lives in Miami, wore a NASA-developed computer attached to his back which signalled his medical condition to a physician on the surface.
